events.title: SOAP 1.2 became a W3C Recommendation
events.summary: The W3C elevated SOAP to a full Recommendation on June 24, 2003 — making XML web services a formal web standard after the SOAP 1.1 Note.
events.about: SOAP 1.2 cleaned up XML Infoset usage, split the spec into messaging framework and adjuncts, and dropped the 'Simple Object Access Protocol' acronym. Enterprise Java (JAX-WS), .NET WCF, and B2B integrations standardized on it before REST+JSON dominated public APIs.

narrative.whyChosen: SOAP 1.2 was the peak formal standardization of XML-RPC-style enterprise web services.
narrative.whyImportant: It gave vendors a normative target for interoperable SOAP stacks in government and banking.
narrative.problemSolved: SOAP 1.1 was only a W3C Note; large integrators needed a full Recommendation with test suites.
